newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus says will improve defences until solution.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus says will improve defences until solution.

text.p: Cyprus will continue to strengthen defences until a way is found to reunify the country and remove Turkish troops occupying a third of the island, President Glafcos Clerides said on Monday.

Clerides, in an address on the eve of the 36th anniversary of Cyprus's independence from Britain, said the republic would push on with implementing a joint defence doctrine with Greece reached in 1993.

Turkish troops occupied the north of the island in 1974 after a brief Greek Cypriot coup inspired by the military ruling Greece. A Turkish Cypriot state declared in northern Cyprus in 1983 is recognised only by Ankara.

"Until the way opens up for a solution, the Cyprus Republic must protect its statehood and its population from the present and clear danger posed by the Attila (Turkish) occupation troops which are armed to the teeth," Clerides said.

The Greek Cypriot side has expressed willingness for face-to-face talks with the Turkish Cypriots, on condition common ground is found on issues such as territorial issues, security and international guarantees, and sovereignty.
Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis is due to arrive in Cyprus on Tuesday for independence day celebrations. He is expected to explore ways for implementing the joint defence doctrine.
